cues.text: JobNet is Katlego's daily career pipeline.
Applying across many boards by hand is slow, and tools that submit on their own are unsafe.
So the job was to shorten research and drafting, without giving the system permission to apply or send mail.
Every day at eight p.m. South African time, it collects public listings.
A hashed sentence embedding ranks each posting against the case studies, and keeps one role per company.
A report of the previous run arrives at three p.m.
A letter is prepared only for a role that clears the ranker.
Then comes the send gate.
Mail leaves only if the address is printed on the posting, the domain resolves, and the letter names that title and company.
Missing addresses are held, not guessed.
The public demo is a read-only shortlist, so visitors cannot trigger applications.
AI assists with ranking and drafting.
A person makes every irreversible decision.
Mercatus Assist and THINK answer a simple question: can a portfolio assistant make a real model call without leaking a key?
Katlego built an ASP.NET Core 8 minimal API in C sharp that calls Gemini through an OpenAI-compatible client, so the provider can change in config.
It runs as a systemd service on an Ubuntu VPS, behind nginx, with the static site behind Cloudflare.
A same-origin proxy keeps the API key on the server.
The client retries with exponential backoff on HTTP 429 and 5xx errors, and public paths have daily caps per IP.
THINK is the React 19, Vite and TypeScript workspace: chat, image, live voice over WebSocket, sites, code and a learning path.
And when the robot's health check fails, the screen says so.
It switches to a labelled demo, because live and demo are not the same state.
Forex Mercatus Codex is a research desk built so it cannot be mistaken for a brokerage.
The hard part is the boundary, not the chart.
It is a Python and Highcharts desk with Chart, Multi, Whales, Flow and Bot views, about eighty-seven megabytes, hosted on a VPS over HTTPS.
Public feeds from Yahoo, Kraken and Binance are fused, and when a feed is down the desk falls back to synthetic tape, which is labelled.
Each browser tab gets its own session-scoped paper bot.
There is a cap of twenty-four sessions, idle sessions expire after two hours, and public mid rates refresh about every sixty seconds.
The health JSON reports paper only.
There are no broker credentials and no order route.
The bot can summarise data and propose a paper action.
A policy gate blocks anything live.
SoundX is a studio you can open in a browser tab.
Most music demos send your audio to someone else's server.
This one does not.
Katlego built it as a browser DAW, with a library, pattern and song views, a mixer and a master bus, all on Web Audio.
A four-step path lets anyone Load Demo, press Play, shape the master, and Generate, with no account and no sign-in.
The AI Producer takes a written request and proposes drums, bass, keys or an arrangement idea.
Generate can listen to the buffer and estimate tempo from onsets.
But it never silently overwrites the session.
The producer proposes, and the session changes only when you apply it.
Synthesis, the optional microphone path, and export all stay in the browser.
Closing the tab leaves nothing on a server.

items.title: Sound Deck AI
items.source: / (Sound Deck AI card) and the Sound Deck AI README

cues.text: Sound Deck AI is Katlego's newest browser studio: an AI drum station with twenty on-device AI tools, a plugin rack, Afro sample packs and twenty-two themes.
Everything works offline with no API key.
Audio stays on the machine, and there is no sign-in.
Tempo and key detection, hum to MIDI, clash-fixing EQ and Mix QA all run in the browser.
The Producer Agent turns a written brief into a full beat in one click, setting the pattern, tempo, swing, pack and plugins.
The sample packs, including Amapiano, Gqom, Afro-house and 808, are original and released as CC0.
Gemini is optional, and if it is switched on it only ever runs on the server.
It is a separate product from SoundX, with its own build, so each can grow without breaking the other.
Mens Mercatus Blueprint is a static portfolio pack: reference drawings and screens, not a live service.
It holds seven schematics.
The overall system architecture, the AI Assist integration pipeline, a Kubernetes topology, the event mode data flow, close friends GPS and ping, compliance gates, and the five jobs pillars.
The event mode screens walk through a signup gate, rate lock, check-in, points, vehicle checklist, no-show, dispute, payout and settings.
Compliance is designed in, with consent gates for minimum wage, POPIA and transport rules documented beside the mockups.
And an AI in every tool plan shows how Assist wires into each surface, refusals included.
It is the thinking behind the products: how a system should behave before a single request goes live.
THINK is a Gemini multimodal workspace: chat, live voice, Net Sites, Net Code, Netzar Protocol and Net Learn, hosted on Mens Mercatus.
It is the live multimodal desk, with chat, image and live paths through the portfolio's Gemini proxy.
Katlego built it as a React 19 workspace, with Vite and TypeScript, a server-side proxy and a live-voice WebSocket relay.
The model key stays on the server.
Live voice and image are capped per IP, and that cap is the control, not a bug.
THINK is a portfolio workspace with caps, not an unlimited production assistant.
And the feed copy inside THINK is product content, not a résumé claim.
Mercatus Assist answers questions about Katlego's work.
Retrieval and intent routing run on your device with a small embedding model.
Gemini writes the answer from the sources it was given, and every claim links back to the page it came from.
When it doesn't know, it says so.
A confidence meter, computed from retrieval similarity, makes a weak match visible instead of hidden.
Paste a job post for a requirement-by-requirement match against the real CV, with honest gaps.
It can explain a project for a recruiter, a business owner or an engineer, in English, isiZulu, Afrikaans or Sesotho.
The conversation lives in this browser tab only.
No cookies, no tracking.
Mercatus Concierge is the guide through Mens Mercatus: a narrative shell over the desks already running, not another product silo.
The journey opens live into existing URLs only, with a status chip for each desk.
It points you to Mercatus Assist, to AI Hawk in JobNet Application, which stays draft-only, to Forex Mercatus Codex, a paper-trading desk with no live-broker claim, to SoundX AI and to THINK.
Where a surface lives only in Mercatus Lab on the Mac Mini, Concierge names it honestly, and shows no fake green.
The builder shell lets you pick a task and jump straight in.
Everything runs in the browser and saves locally, with no account and no credits.
Mocks stay mocks: chat replies, scores and the portal are local demos, with no payments, no real sign-in and no AI calls.
JobNet Application is one app for the whole job-search loop.
JobNet scrapes public LinkedIn and Glassdoor listings off this site, and the shortlist comes from its read-only public API.
Sentence embeddings, running in a background worker on your device, compare each requirement with real CV evidence, and BM25 takes over instantly when the model isn't loaded.
AI Hawk, formerly Drop Net, then drafts a tailored cover note and CV synopsis for the role you pick.
It runs from templates on this device, with no model call, and nothing is stored or sent.
You review the draft, then copy it or forward it by email yourself.
Nothing is ever sent or applied for automatically.
Mens Mercatus Fleet is a maintenance desk for South African vehicle fleets.
Katlego built a FastAPI server in Python with a SQLite store, a rule engine for minor-repair approval and a NumPy price regressor trained on 160 fictional invoices.
Repairs up to two thousand five hundred rand, and within eight and a half percent of the fair price, are approved by rule.
A counter or manager band runs to fifteen thousand rand, and anything above goes to an executive.
Fault to Repair turns a fault code and a workshop quote into a fair price in rand and an approval tier.
Fifteen Fleet Intelligence tools cover warranty, service reminders, pre-trip checks, fuel slips, compliance, theft alerts and driver coaching.
WhatsApp and Teams messages are drafts and virtual cards are mock only, so a person signs off every action.
Every vehicle, workshop and price is example data.
This is a local demo, not a deployed product, and four hundred and six automated tests pass.
